questions.topic: One-sided limits and the two-sided limit
questions.stem: An architect's brief: f(x)=x/|x| for x≠0; right limit at 0 is 1; student says left limit also 1; error?

options.misconception: misses sign — treating "No error" as the answer
swaps — treating "Right limit should be -1" as the answer
selects "Limit exists" instead of "Left limit is -1, not 1"

questions.explanation: The rule that settles this one-sided limits and the two-sided limit item is: Left side negative. That is why "Left limit is -1, not 1" is right. The option "No error" (misses sign — treating "No error" as the answer) does not satisfy the rule.
